denial.carcText: The time limit for filing has expired.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 19357 (breast reconstruction with tissue expander) with date of service 2026-08-21. CARC 29: The time limit for filing has expired. Payer remark: The claim was received more than 90 days after the date of service.

criteria.text: Documented mastectomy for breast cancer, or prophylactic mastectomy for a qualifying risk, with reconstruction requested by the patient. Reconstruction after a covered mastectomy is a mandated benefit under the Women’s Health and Cancer Rights Act.
An operative plan for staged reconstruction (tissue expander placement followed by implant exchange) appropriate to the patient’s radiation status and tissue quality.
Medical clearance for the planned surgery is documented.

chart.text: Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

From the breast surgeon: left total mastectomy performed 5 months ago for a 2.1 centimeter invasive ductal carcinoma, sentinel nodes negative, margins clear. She has completed adjuvant chemotherapy and wishes to proceed with reconstruction.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

33 year old woman referred by the breast surgeon for reconstruction. Went over expanders versus flaps, she prefers the expander route, fewer operations and no donor site. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now, hypertension on lisinopril, seasonal allergies. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works in a warehouse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Status post left mastectomy 5 months ago for a 2.1 centimeter invasive ductal. Done with chemo. She wants reconstruction and has thought hard about it. No radiation planned per oncology. Good skin envelope, no infection, mastectomy flap healed. Plan is a left tissue expander under the pectoralis now, exchange to a permanent implant in about 6 months, and a right lift for symmetry later.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 13 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Back with her sister to go over the plan again. Questions answered. Ready to schedule. Vitals today 112 over 73, pulse 87.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 201, LDL 122, HDL 42, triglycerides 192. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.8, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
Pre-op. Cleared by her PCP, letter in the chart, labs and EKG fine. Consent signed for left tissue expander placement.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

expected.note: CARC 29 is an administrative denial the chart cannot answer: the remedy is proof of timely submission, not a medical necessity appeal.
